title: A ring the rods make themselves: with the surfactant source restricted to rod pixels and chis 3 -> 5, the ringed nematic rods' s-layer passes the signed-distance L3 test in 99-100% of body-frames on 3 seeds and at a 1.5x grid; chis=0 removes it; but no rod swims 3 body lengths and then divides
summary: c11's ringed active-nematic rods, with the one change the question asked for (src = ks [phi>0]: every surfactant molecule is made on a rod pixel, none by the bath) and the adsorption drift raised from chis=3 to 5 (at chis=3 the rod-only ring passes in only 63% of body-frames, as c21's source-split copy predicted). By signed distance to phi=0 (c21's sd_individuals.py), 99/100/99% of body-frames on seeds 0/1/2 (T=1000) pass both rim/core and rim/out >= 1.5 (medians 2.7-2.8 and 7.8-8.1), and 100% at a 1.5x grid (dx=0.6667, 192^2, shells in world units; 98% with pixel shells), where bodies still nucleate (25) and divide (15 persistent splits) once the initial noise keeps its power per unit area. The chis=0 ablation gives a diffuse fill (0%, rim/core 0.74). Bodies are unchanged from c11's world (22/13/22 persistent splits, gen 3-4, M up to 3.5-5.7 labkit body lengths in the tail), and the zeta=0 twin gives static round droplets with no splits and no motion, so D and M need the active stress while the passive ring does not. Limit: by labkit's own tracker no track that ends in a division has moved >= 3 body lengths (max 2.76 labkit, 1.66 by rod length), so M and D are not on the same individuals yet; the ring is a quasi-equilibrium coating that does no work.

finding.operator: surfactant made only by the rods (src = ks [phi>0]) with adsorption drift chis*Ds*s*grad(1-phi^2), chis=5
finding.control: chis=0 ablation (diffuse fill), 1.5x grid, 3 seeds; zeta=0 twin for M and D
finding.result: rod-made ring passes rim/core and rim/out >= 1.5 in 99/100/99% of body-frames (seeds 0/1/2) and 100% at 1.5x; chis=0: 0%, rim/core 0.74; chis=3: 63%; swim >= 3 BL then divide: 0 tracks on 4 runs (max 2.76 labkit BL)
